reads_as: code's arithmetic on the frozen input: the cases a design needs, sized on today's estimate and its spread (a normal approximation), and how often today's design would read the other way if the truth equals today's estimate; it plans a run, it tests nothing
sided: one-sided at the snapshot's level: a bound centred on today's figure sits wholly on today's side of the line, which clears the line where today's figure passes (settles: clears) and confirms the miss where it misses (settles: misses); cases_needed is the size at which half such designs do if the truth equals today's figure, cases_needed_80 the size at which four in five do. A page prints two-sided intervals, which need more: cases_needed_two_sided and cases_needed_two_sided_80 are the same sizes for the two-sided interval at the level. Each size counts what count_of says the count counts: trials, not cases, on a repeated design
